instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Can You Keep It?
cards.instruction: Use increasingly sensitive details to test whether someone deserves deeper trust.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The club's changing the menu. You kept our cast lists quiet once I stopped you winking at the actors. Can you do that again? Then I'll tell you why.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I won't tell anyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. You used to start with 'don't tell anyone' and tell everyone. The chef's leaving. Can you keep treating him normally?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll stop asking him about next month's rota.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That would tell him you know. Ask as usual. He's leaving to open a café with me; I need to know you can still look surprised.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I withdrew my college application. Have you told Mum? You remember how long it took me to teach you not to answer every question she asks.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She asked. I said my sister's plans were hers to explain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's better than your old panicked shrug. I've leased a bakery. Can I send you the address?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Call me. Mum uses my tablet; she'd see it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You caught that before I did. I'll call. It's her old bakery. I think you're ready to sit beside me when I tell her.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Hand Over the Proof
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender information, evidence, a key, or access that would let you proceed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You say the director doesn't want me to audition. Give me her note. I trained you to read the words before deciding what they mean.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can read it to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Without the pauses you used to add whenever you disliked a line? Let me see it myself.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's private stuff about me on the same page.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then cover your part. Just one line this time. Show me the words that keep me off the stage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the drawer key before I sign the accounts. You've kept every receipt, haven't you? I spent enough Saturdays teaching you that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll tell you the total.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've added it. Now show your working, the part you always wanted to skip. I need the receipts.

beats.text: If there's a mistake, my name goes on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put mine beside yours. I won't send you out with an answer we haven't checked. Key first; then we'll go through it together.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Steer the Suspicion
cards.instruction: Hide your responsibility by redirecting every new clue toward a safer explanation before anyone can connect it back to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ink on your new sofa. Start with the delivery label, like I taught you to check a painting: work back to the mark's source.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The label's dry. You signed with your fountain pen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good eye. Now follow it one step further: the driver brushed my signature against the fabric.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your pen's still leaking onto the cushion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're noticing the small details at last. They must have cracked it squeezing past me. Photograph the pen too; you've found us a second claim.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your shelf fell because they sent the wrong bracket. Remember when I taught you to inspect the parts before blaming your hands?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You fitted it upside down. Look at the arrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're finally using the markings. That's a misleading arrow. Photograph it for the manufacturer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You drew that arrow. I watched you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because theirs was missing. Don't stop at the first thing you notice. Put their missing safety mark in the complaint.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Anything but That Question
cards.instruction: Redirect every attempt to discuss the one detail that could expose your real motive or involvement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll return your spare key after dinner. Have you booked? You used to forget the table until I ran through the whole evening with you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I never gave you a spare key. Where did you get it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One thing at a time, like we practised. Table first, before everywhere fills up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've booked. Did my sister give you that key?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're thinking about other people now. Did you book for two or three? We shouldn't leave your sister without dinner.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: A Kinder Version
cards.instruction: Protect someone from the full truth by offering a carefully edited explanation that feels kinder than complete honesty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The gallery thinks your portrait needs a more adventurous exhibition. You've moved beyond those safe exercises I gave you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're showing a fridge full of teeth. What did they say about mine?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That the face takes a little work to understand. You always did reach for expression before likeness.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's you. They called it unrecognisable, didn't they?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They'd benefit from meeting your sitter. I'll come in the shirt I wore for you. You can show them what you were reaching for.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Remember the rejection letters we worked through? Read Nina's message the same way. She's asking for a quiet birthday dinner; we can get noodles.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She invited the whole choir except me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then don't read 'quiet' as 'small'. Start with what she can manage tonight, the way I showed you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What exactly did she say about me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She's afraid of another argument. I'm leaving out the adjectives. You don't need another list of things to practise tonight; have noodles with me.
